过去给 Google 高估值是建立他是现金牛：广告利润率高、资本开支相对较低、持续回购股票。现在这个特征在消失。现在广告不行了，换赛道，估值要重新定价，在趋势确立前，一定是低 PE。  

而对于谷歌云业务，目前算下来回本周期在 3-5年，而服务器的平均寿命也就6年。在悲观情形下，接近五年才回本，回本后只剩约一年的超额回报期，六年 IRR 约 11%。这仅略高于 Alphabet 的资本成本（10.4%）。  

典型的高风险，低收益，上限很低的生意，属于广告业务不行了只能拉着股东背水一战。

我相信 Google 这个体量虽然不会彻底完蛋，但现在市面上一大把低风险高收益的生意。
Elysium 在上线之初就会有一个完整的生态系统，由其他链的高置信度项目背书。

这位30年几乎没有出现过年度亏损、做过索罗斯旗下基金操盘手的投资大佬，在X上异常低调 @standuquesne ，但有个加密玩家们喜闻乐见的投资理论，那就是：

“先上车，在研究”。

@BTCdayu 大宇老师的公众号在5个月前，曾系统的整理了德鲁肯米勒公开的访谈和各类投资发言，其中就提到了这一点，原文是这么说的：
------
“德鲁肯米勒自己更通俗地表述为“Buy first, analyze later”。

逻辑是这样的：“市场是聪明的、很快的，而且因为通讯和技术，越来越快。如果我听到一个我喜欢的想法，去花两三个月去分析它，我可能会错过大部分行情，然后心理上被瘫痪——一个 100 块的股票你看着它涨到 160，即使你知道它会到 400，你的脑子也会卡住，等回调。”

所以他的做法是，先建一个有意义但不致命的仓位（比如 1–2% NAV 的探索仓，看好的话才扩到 20–25%），然后开始真正做研究。

如果发现自己错了，就卖掉；如果对了，就金字塔加仓。

NVIDIA 那笔交易就是经典案例。

他后来回忆，早在 2022 年前后，他的年轻分析师就不断提醒他：Stanford、MIT 一类顶尖工程师的兴趣，正在从 crypto 转向 AI。这是第一个信号。

当时他并没有真正理解英伟达在 AI 里的位置，仍大致把它看成一家游戏显卡公司；但他听完团队说“这就是 AI 最直接的表达式”后，先买了一笔不算大的仓位。

不久后，ChatGPT 发布。他后来承认：“那纯粹是运气。”更准确地说，NVDA 当时已经从 2021 年三百多美元的高点跌到 2022 年底约 150 美元附近，”。

他先建仓，之后才真正开始深入研究。这正是索罗斯的那条老规则——先投资，再调查。”
-----

继被标普 500 拒之门外后，Strategy 的资本飞轮正迎来传统金融体系最严峻的一次审查。

国际指数编制巨头 MSCI 定于 11 月 11 日公布成分股筛选结果。由于新规重点排查“缺乏实质运营资产”的投资载体，Strategy 以及日股 Metaplanet 等比特币金库概念股，均被列入潜在剔除名单。

最直接的冲击是抛压。

据摩根大通测算，若被剔除出 MSCI，跟踪该指数的被动基金将带来约 28 亿美元的卖盘；若其他主流指数跟进，抛售总额恐攀升至 88 亿美元。

但真正致命的其实是融资生命线。Strategy 过去能够持续大规模加仓比特币，高度依赖在美股溢价增发股票、优先股以及可转债。

指数被动配置资金此前是其重要的买盘底仓，一旦失去这层支撑，加上市场对股权稀释的担忧，未来继续通过“发债发股买币”的资本飞轮将急剧承压。

quote.text:
Ledger 硬件钱包的供应链安全问题似乎还在扩大。

之前我们报道过，马来西亚的硬件钱包授权经销商CryptoBilis 所售的 Ledger 中，有设备被植入隐藏 LTE/eSIM 板监控屏幕捕获助记词，导致大规模资金被盗。

现在也有社区用户反馈，欧洲大型电子零售商 MediaMarkt 卖出的一台 Ledger Nano X 被拆开后，发现内部多出了不属于原厂设计的额外电路板和线路。

这台设备是用户 @0xJohannes_大约两周前在实体店买的，不过目前资金还没有被盗。

也有懂行技术老哥查看拆机照片后指出，拆机后设备里的天线标注为“欧亚版本”，说明攻击者可能针对不同地区的手机网络频率，做了专门适配的植入板，而不是随便改装的。

此外，在 Ledger 目前针对钱包安全问题的官方说明贴下，也有用户报告拆开 Ledger Stax 后，在屏幕下方发现了原厂设备根本不需要的蜂窝网络模块，用于远程传输数据。

但这些零星事件目前都没有得到 Ledger 的官方证实与回应。

不过作为硬件钱包的持有者来说，如果不是从 Ledger 官网直接购买的设备，最好不要初始化，或尽快生成新助记词转移资产，并参考官方拆解指南检查内部有无异常元件。

现在做AI相关的事情，很多人会有种感觉：赛道很拥挤，方向越来越难找。

模型层竞争激烈，纯软件套壳的溢价在快速收窄，很多创业者开始怀疑，是不是已经没有真正有空间的机会了？

其实未必。真正的瓶颈，正在从模型本身向外扩散。

硅谷创投风向标 Y Combinator 最新发布的「创业愿望清单（Request for Startups，RFS）」就明确指出，下一波更扎实的机会，可能就藏在“重一点、难一点、更靠近物理世界”的地方。

以下是YC重点关注的11个方向：

• 商业太空：Starship可能让入轨成本下降一个数量级甚至100倍后，哪些新商业模式会变得可行；

• 普惠专家：用AI把普通人变成能胜任专业工作的“$15/小时专家”，打破稀缺证书和经验的限制；

• 本土机器人：从稀土磁体、电机、减速器到传感器和芯片，重建美国机器人供应链；

• 深度写作：专门优化文笔和风格的模型，对抗当前LLM写作越来越平、越来越像机器的问题；

• 政务Plaid：打通跨系统的收入、税务、居住验证，一次验证、多处可用，降低摩擦与欺诈空间（美国福利欺诈规模约$5000亿/年）；

• 基建华尔街：为机器人、GPU集群、数据中心等重资产提供新的融资、租赁和证券化工具；

• 垂直模型：面向制造、能源、生物等垂直领域的专用基础模型，用更低算力做到强性能；

• 市政AI：用AI加速建筑审批、检查、许可和公共记录处理（美国约有1.9万个城市，潜在市场巨大）；

• 算力供应链：变压器交期长达数年，开关柜、液冷、特种钢材等成为新瓶颈，供应链各环节都有机会；

• 局域网AI：为军工、银行、医院、核电等无法上云的场景，提供本地部署的模型、工具和硬件；

• 主权模型：帮助企业从“租用云端API”转向基于自身数据和工作流、可自主训练和进化的私有模型。

Strap in and consider this my official update on the kinetiq:native thesis, specifically regarding @Enter_Elysium.

Best way to do this is to refute some arguments I've seen:

1. "L2's are parasitic"

It's very lazy to compare Elysium to other L2s from the past. Robinhood Chain has generated a little over $50m in fees, of which $5m went to Arbitrum, and a whopping...$70k went to $ETH blob fees.

HyperEVM hyperliquid:native fees are burnt, whereas sequencer fees on Elysium go to kinetiq:native buys and builders (more on this later), but HyperEVM fees only account less than 1% of Hyperliquid total revenue. Papertrade is actually much more directly parasitic to hyperliquid:native; HyperEVM fees are peanuts even if Elysium vamped them entirely.

An under appreciated dynamic that a lot of people don't know is that HyperEVM USDC applies to AQAv2 hyperliquid:native revenue too, and USDC on Elysium will as well. Assuming the HyperEVM burns around $25k of hyperliquid:native a day, every additional $1b USDC that Elysium onboards in TVL would burn 4x that same amount due to AQAv2. 

For reference, Solana has ~$7.5bn USDC and Base has $5b. Robinhood chain is predominantly USDG, which they monetize on, and ETH obviously gets nothing from. Imagine if Base contributed to $175m (3.5% of $5b) of value accrual to $ETH via their USDC TVL...maybe my $5k/7k $ETH calls would actually hit then 🙃

Beyond this, the entire selling point of Elysium is that it sits adjacent to HyperCore. propAMM's are functionally impossible on HyperEVM now due to the 1s block time (amongst other reasons). Additionally, on the HyperEVM, you can only read Hypercore price, not order book depth. 

As a result, Solana does 25-50x the spot trading volume that Hypercore/HyperEVM handle. If Elysium can eat even a moderate chunk of on chain spot volume from Solana, especially in tokenized RWAs, the implications for corresponding hedging flows to Hyperliquid are enormous. 

Elysium explicity enables net new flow and TVL to Hyperliquid, both of which are very accretive to hyperliquid:native itself. I would not be surprised if Elysium directly contributes an additional low 9 figure ARR for hyperliquid:native in 2027. 

2. "L2's are bad investments and down only tokens"

As stated above, $ARB made about $5m so far from Robinhood Chain. Of that amount, a whopping...zero dollars made it to tokenholders. No buybacks, no burns, nothing.

50% of Elysium sequencer fees are directed at kinetiq:native buybacks. Even if you assume that Elysium only generates half the current sequencer fees of the current ghost town that is the HyperEVM, that'd still more than double their current revenue. 

Currently, kinetiq:native buybacks as a % of market cap are about 1.5%, compared to 4-5% for hyperliquid:native. If Elysium generates only half of the sequencer fees of the current HyperEVM ($5m/yr), they'd be retiring token off the market at the same rate that hyperliquid:native does relative to market cap.

If Elysium can do closer to 50-75% of Base annualized sequencer fees ($30m), they'd be doing kinetiq:native buybacks at double the rate of hyperliquid:native as a % of market cap.

This is completely negating a likely increase in kHYPE TVL and other revenue streams (which there are numerous), like from launchpads like @AscendLaunch.

Ascend actually deserves their own section because they've commited to doing 30% of gross revenue as kinetiq:native buy/burns (50% to buys, 60% of that to burn). $PONS has generated $200m revenue in the last 2 months, but is currently only annualizing about $125m revenue, so we'll use a very conservative ~10% of the more conservative number. That'd add another $4m of kinetiq:native buybacks, which brings buyback yield/mcap well into the double digit %, over double hyperliquid:native.

3. "Why would there be activity on Elysium if there wasn't on the HyperEVM?"

Probably because the HyperEVM operates at the speed of smoke signals and has 0 support from Hyperliquid. 

You have @Uniswap, @fomo, @Pumpfun etc all announcing integrations and deployments on Elysium day 1 after ignoring the HyperEVM all this time. @0xOmnia and the @Kinetiq_xyz team is putting on a master class in distribution, and you're seeing it play out this week. 

Jeff and company are focusing on building the best perps platform in the world, and that's great, but this hands off approach has come at the expense of any support or curation of an on chain ecosystem. 

That's left a massive gap that other chains have filled, but Elysium can bring all that activity back into the "house of all finance". Having a team that's fully dedicated to making this a reality will look nothing like the lack of attention the HyperEVM received.

4. "It'll be a flash in the pan memecoin chain and die out just like RHC activity has"

This is more speculative and it's hard to say. Elysium could have an epic and unsustainable PvElysium memecoin season by inheriting some of the wealth effect from both hyperliquid:native and kinetiq:native. Obviously this would absolutely moon kinetiq:native from sequencer fees/Ascend revenue, but that's shortlived.

Lively trenches aren't mutually exclusive with a real and innovative DeFi ecosystem though. As I mentioned before, Elysium will be uniquely able to plug in with, leverage, and read Hyperliquid orderbooks and liquidity. DeFi applications that couldn't be built anywhere else are made possible here. 

A performant general purpose blockchain adjacent to HyperCore is the natural home to propAMM and HFT arbitrage against HIP3, which incentivizes deeply liquid spot RWA markets, which enables much higher LTV lending, which enables unique structured products and DeFi primitives to be built.

I do imagine that the trenches are built before more serious innovation comes about, but an important note here is that builders are getting 25% of sequencer fees as well. What builder wouldn't want to deploy on a new ecosystem, adjacent to the most successful app in crypto history, with a built in rev share agreement with the chain itself? Based on my conversations with Ascend and Montra, lots of serious teams want to build, not just memecoin deployers.

TLDR: It's not that complicated guys. kinetiq:native is a $120m mcap token that has a very clear path to buyback % yields multiples higher than hyperliquid:native, with an unprecedented ecosystem flywheel. It's both beta to hyperliquid:native and enhances the hyperliquid:native bull case. It might be the most asymmetric bet in crypto right now, and it's not conditional on some long shot thesis, just that there will be a large on chain ecosystem for the most important app in crypto. 

Maybe it's a flop and a sell the news event on launch...or maybe it's all the best parts of Base/Hood sequencer fees combined with the revenue streams of $PUMP, $CAKE, solana:jtojtomepa8beP8AuQc6eXt5FriJwfFMwQx2v2f9mCL, ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 etc and heads towards billions of TVL and 9 figure annual revenue.

If you pattern match too hard to "L2 bad" or "HyperEVM sucks", it's from a place of being too 🏳️‍🌈🐻-pilled and/or lazy research.

As someone who has personally spent $500k / mo+ on Google Ads for years, I can tell you with certainty: 

This revenue growth in Search is artificial & extremely unhealthy for Google’s business long term

Search volumes are declining as legacy search is being increasingly cannibalized by non-monetized LLM queries

Google’s response? 

Manufacture revenue growth via short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics. I.e. charge advertisers more for lower quality clicks, including clicks they do not want and explicitly did not approve Google to charge them for

A few examples to illustrate: 

For all of its history until recently, Google operated on a 2nd price auction model

I.e. if you bid $5 CPC and the next highest bidder bids $1 CPC, Google charged you $1.01 for the click (one penny more than the 2nd highest bidder) rather than the $5 you bid

This was a genius move by Google early on as it incentivizes advertisers to input their true maximum willingness to pay rather than trying to play the game of bidding low and constantly adjusting to try to stay just ahead of the next highest bidder while still not paying too much

However recently, Google silently deprecated the 2nd price auction and began charging advertisers as much as their bid and budget caps allow, regardless of what anyone else is bidding

It’s a short-sighted cash grab at the expense of the long term health of the  advertiser ecosystem

Making thing worse, Google also recently nerfed keyword targeting precision

Google previously had precise keyword targeting settings that allowed advertisers pick individual search phrases to bid on, defined down to the character w/ exact match or phrase match targeting 

This was one of the core features that made search advertising magic, enabling advertisers to run extremely precise campaigns based on exactly what their target customer typed 

But now, even if you bid on a specific term or phrase using the strictest exact 
-match targeting settings, Google will show your ad across 1000’s of unrelated keywords, labeling them as as “exact match (close variant)” 

The definition of “close variant” means whatever they want it to and changes constantly. The result is advertisers get billed for clicks that are totally irrelevant to their business and that their targeting settings explicitly forbid Google from targeting. Google does it anyway and there’s no ability to turn this off

So now exact match is broad match, and broad match is just meaningless spam

This is all very bad for advertisers, but for Google, it allows them to show your ad and bill you for clicks across 1000x more searches that were previously going unmonetized (mainly because they’re garbage queries no one wants) 

This is how you grow revenue atop declining search volumes 

Lastly, and perhaps most egregiously, Google quietly stopped respecting budget caps by a factor of 2x. For example campaigns we’ve been running for years with $1000 daily budget caps suddenly began spending $2000+ per day 

And the extra spend is entirely on the garbage keywords Google arbitrarily throws in as “exact match (close variants)” which have no value to our business, but can’t be turned off

Google offers no refunds nor any recourse for overspend or spend on keywords you explicitly did not target

These are not the actions of a healthy business. These are the actions of company whose core business is in decline but desperately needs to pump quarterly earnings so Wall Street will continue to fund insane capex while hopefully looking through their rapidly deteriorating negative free cash flow 

Google operated a benevolent monopoly for the better part of 25 yrs

Meaning the value Google captured from Search was but a small fraction of the value it created, and that spread produced a potential energy that justified expectations of high earnings growth far, far into the future 

This is now no longer the case

At the alter of AI capex, Google is sacrificing the golden goose

本季度不及预期是因为供货延迟的问题，不是公司主动下调。
